purpose: Continue the fresh Development search from the already frozen v4 metadata inventory after both candidates eligible under the narrow v1 selector have been consumed as selections: #64675 was overlap-blocked and #64575 was source-qualified but its assigned 14B attempt did not run at the resource gate. This protocol does not reuse either task.
hypothesis: A deterministic rank over the remaining metadata rows that passed the v4 coarse screen can identify another candidate for a separate family-overlap review, source qualification, and feasibility decision without inspecting task content during selection.

selection.eligibility: Only rows with coarse_screen=provisional_for_manual_review, an empty screen_reasons list, complete changed_paths, a test path in the merged diff, state=MERGED, qualification_status=UNQUALIFIED, split_assignment=UNASSIGNED, and task_family_overlap=NOT_ASSESSED are eligible.

excluded_identities.reason: Previously selected by v1 and blocked by its frozen overlap review; no reuse.
Previously selected by v2 and source-qualified; its distinct 14B attempt was NOT RUN at the resource gate. No reuse under this new-task continuation.

selection.rank: SHA256(UTF8(rank_domain + '|' + repository + '#' + pull_request_number)); ascending bytewise hex order.

stop_rules: Verify every frozen input hash before ranking; stop on any mismatch.
Do not fetch or inspect PR bodies, discussions, patches, source, tests, task prompts, or grader assets during this metadata-only selection.

Select exactly the first ranked eligible identity after the two explicit exclusions; do not manually rerank or substitute if the selected candidate later overlaps, fails qualification, or is infeasible.
Keep the selected candidate UNQUALIFIED and UNASSIGNED; this selection does not authorize source access, assignment, inference, training, or Held-Out access.
If selection yields no candidate, preserve that outcome and freeze a separate protocol before any broader inventory search.
limitations: The v4 metadata scan covers six repositories and one UTC date, not a global task inventory.
Recent merge date does not establish public-pretraining independence.
Metadata screening does not establish family independence, source-level qualification, CPU feasibility, or model capability.
This selection provides no evidence of a successful coding repair or policy learning.
